questions.stem: Why does the rate of photosynthesis decrease at very high temperatures?

options.text: The plant absorbs too much water
Light energy is converted to heat energy
Enzymes involved in photosynthesis become denatured
Carbon dioxide becomes less soluble in water

questions.explanation: At very high temperatures, the enzymes that catalyse the reactions of photosynthesis become denatured. Their active sites change shape, so they can no longer function.
